title: Ordinary condensed-coefficient module pullback is strong monoidal
statement: Use [def-weil-pbc-residue-exchange-comparison-interface]. For any condensed commutative coefficient ring Λ and any scheme morphism f, construct a strong monoidal structure on the actual internal-module pullback (f)^*⟦Λ⟧. More generally, a strong braided monoidal functor G preserving the balanced coequalizers, and an isomorphism of commutative ring objects ρ:S→G(R), give a strong monoidal structure on Mod.mapModComap ρ. The module tensorator and unit are explicit maps with all naturality, unit and associativity laws proved.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), Proposition 6.8.11(3), Remark 6.8.15; explicit formal coefficient and adjunction argument

proof.text: Expose the balanced coequalizer as a cofork of module objects. Forgetting the module action creates this colimit, which identifies the coequalizer tensor functor with the existing monoidal tensor. Prove the presentation formulas for the unitors.

Use tensorLeftCompMapModComapIso to construct the tensor comparison, and the inverse ring isomorphism for the unit comparison. Their composites with presentation epimorphisms are the ambient monoidal tensor and unit maps. Prove naturality, both unit laws, and associativity by cancellation of those epimorphisms and the ambient strong monoidal coherence laws.

Assemble CoreMonoidal. The ordinary coefficient pullback is mapMod followed by scalar extension along the coefficient-pullback isomorphism; extendScalarsIsoComapInv identifies it with mapModComap. Transport the proved monoidal structure along that explicit isomorphism.
